subject: Size of geom_tippoint zero does still give bubble

messages.author: 424e4c78b7fd4c1e
messages.subject: Size of geom_tippoint zero does still give bubble
parts:
Hi,

I am using ggtree to visualize the distribution of T cells between samples based on T cell receptor CDR3b sequence similarity. 

I calculate my distance matrix using Needleman-Wunsch global alignment, and then I use neighbor-joining (phangorn::NJ) to create my phylotree (my input here is a matrix symmetrical matrix with colnames = rownames = clone sequence for clone 1 to n). I can plot this tree nicely and I even get nice bubbles by using geom_tippoint (I point the size parameter to a vector determining the size of the bubble). However, geom_tippoint will give me a small bubble also for zeros in vector. This is not desirable. If the abundance is zero, i want no bubble. I even tried using geom_tippoint size = 0, and I still see small bubbles on the tips of my plot.

I attached a figure for you guys.

Please help!

messages.author: 424e4c78b7fd4c1e
messages.subject: Re: Size of geom_tippoint zero does still give bubble
parts:
And I have also tried using scale_size_area(). My code is as following:

method_plot = 'circular'
i=100
line_width = 0.1
margins = c(-3,-2,-3,-2)
ggtree(nj_nw_distances, layout = method_plot, size=line_width, ladderize=T) + 
  geom_tippoint(color="yellow", alpha=1, size=(i*(rowSums(freq_pivot[,21:28])/sum(freq_pivot[,21:28])))) +
  scale_size_area() +
  theme(plot.margin = unit(margins, "cm"))

Where freq pivot is a dataframe containing my frequencies for each sequence. (all other crappy code in size is due to normalization). However, this vector contains only 8 values > 0.

Thanks,
Nils
